whatWasResolved.corpus: Recovered. The HTTP 403 was this session's own GitHub repository scope, not the token and not GitHub: the proxy answered "GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session. Use add_repo to request access." After add_repo for Roger-LegalEase/legalease-source-artifacts with access push, the release endpoint answers 200 and scripts/rcap-corpus/bootstrap-private-corpus.sh installs 51 jurisdictions / 499 files / 329 PDFs with the archive SHA-256 verified. Captain was right that it was never a permissions problem; the first FIX-A diagnosis and FIX-B's were wrong the same way.

westHost.diagnosis: westParticipantInstructions is defined at line 1524 and its writer was never defined and is never imported. Both call sites write participant-instructions.md, so every AZ and every CA family crashes there. buildAz crashes after production-field-map.json and the census are rewritten and before any fixture is rendered, which leaves a half-rebuilt overlay if it is not restored.
westHost.alsoNeeded: the CA path calls a pikepdf bridge and fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pikepdf' before it reaches writeText. python3 -m pip install pikepdf fixes that; the preflight does not check for it, so a CA lane learns after it has already cleared its output directory.

eastHost.diagnosis: the fields it names are exactly the ones the fact allowlist binds. reproducedOn: nj_indictable_conviction-set (NJ-CN-10557/canonical; arrestOff1, guiltyDt, guiltyCrt, DefAddr2, DefBirthDt, arrest1Dt among others)

blockerCorrection.whyThisExplainsTheStaleness: commit 9a484a6 (lane S1) extended both hosts' fact allowlists and added the west host's participant-instructions writer on 2026-08-31, and no family was rebuilt afterwards. These two defects are why: the west host crashes on the new writer and the east host's new writes produce no ink. Every overlay in the fleet has been stale since that commit, and no builder lane could have rebuilt one.
blockerCorrection.consequenceForTheseRows: the rows below stay STOPPED and their reason is unchanged in substance -- a repair that needs new ink is a rebuild, and no rebuild completes. What changed is why: not a missing corpus, but two defects in hosts this lane does not own and must not edit while other lanes build from them.
blockerCorrection.whatFixANeeds: a lane that owns the two hosts. The west host needs its missing writeText helper and pikepdf in the build environment; the east host needs the finalizer to actually draw the newly allowlisted fields, or those bindings withdrawn until it can. Once either host builds, FIX-A's stopped rows are ordinary rebuilds.

rootCause.finding: the S1 fact allowlist and the shared semantic finalizer disagree, on every field S1 added, and the finalizer refuses all of them.
rootCause.evidence: reports/actual-writes.json in the committed nj_indictable_conviction-set build records 173 fields refused with reason classified_unwritable_by_role, category role. Every one of the twelve terminal names SHARED_EXACT_FACT_ALLOWLIST and the family allow bind is in that refused list: DefName, DefAddrStr, DefAddr2, DefAddr3, ExpungeCntyName, DefBirthDt, origCaseNums, arrestOff1, arrest1Dt, arrest1CaseNum, guiltyDt and guiltyCrt. Not one of them appears in the written list.
rootCause.mechanism: the host's own decisionBasis says it: "shared exact terminal-name fact allowlist; shared semantic finalizer still controls". The allowlist promotes the field to candidate_write, the finalizer refuses it by role, and the build then asserts because the map claimed a write that produced no appearance. That is why the rebuild fails and why no overlay has been rebuilt since commit 9a484a6.
rootCause.whyItMattersForTheseRows: if the finalizer is right that these fields are not writable by role, then the treatment this lane applied to them -- declare the blank required before filing and name it for the participant -- is the correct final answer and not a placeholder, and the repair is to withdraw the allowlist entries rather than to make the finalizer draw them. If the allowlist is right, the finalizer's role classification is what needs to change. Which way it resolves is a legal and product question about whether, for example, the defendant's own name on the New Jersey petition is the platform's to write, and a repair lane does not decide it.
rootCause.whatWouldSettleIt: one owner of the shared finalizer and the two hosts reconciling the role classification against the allowlist, field by field, and stating which side governs. Until then no east or west family can be rebuilt, and the stopped rows in these four returns stay stopped.
rootCause.notDecidedHere: this lane changed neither host, neither allowlist, nor the finalizer. Other lanes in this shift build from the same files.

correction.whatIGotWrong: this return recorded classified_unwritable_by_role as the root cause of the east-host rebuild failure. That reading came from the committed reports/actual-writes.json, which records 173 such refusals from an older build. The live run does not fail there.
correction.whatIsActuallyObserved: the live failure is the appearance assertion on a handful of address, date-of-birth, charge and court fields whose values the finalizer reports writing and which never reach the flattened appearance streams. On nj_indictable_conviction-set this lane observed arrestOff1, guiltyDt, guiltyCrt, DefAddr2, DefBirthDt and arrest1Dt; Captain's run of nj_arrest_no_conviction-set observed arrestOff1, dismissDt, dismissCrt, DefAddr2, DefAddr3, DefBirthDt and arrest1Dt. DefName is in neither live list.
correction.standing: the failure and the field lists stand as reported. The mechanism does not: cross-referencing an older actual-writes record to explain a live assertion was an inference, and it was stated here as a finding. It is withdrawn.
correction.separately: Roger Roman decided on 2026-09-01 that the participant's own name is a platform-written participant fact. DefName is already bound to participant.full_legal_name in the shared allowlist, so no allowlist change follows from it, and no artifact can show it until the host finishes a build.

noteOnOwnership: FIX07's owned paths include the nj-arrest-no-conviction overlay but not scripts/build-census-v1-nj_arrest_no_conviction-set.mjs, which is the shared east host itself and carries that family's name. The repairs here are in the overlay only; the host was read and never written.

whatIsMissing.whatWouldUnblockIt: A container that mounts private/source-imports/Nationwide_Recovery_Pool_2026-09-02. The defects themselves are engineering defects in the shared Alabama and Illinois build hosts and need no legal or source research; they need the source bytes in order to be rebuilt, rehashed and re-measured.
whatIsMissing.whyNoCodeWasLandedAnyway: The mapping fixes are writable without the bytes, but they cannot be built, rehashed or measured here. Landing an unbuilt code change into hosts that other, unblocked containers rebuild would put this family's committed artifacts out of step with its builder and would move families this lane does not hold. That is the failure mode that left the Ohio companion undelivered in the first place.
